exact_statement: For finite uniform Boolean signs f and degree<=d phase P, let delta=Pr[f=-1], gamma=2^(1-d)-4delta>=0, a be full affine/character minimum influence, r the affine spectral rank of P, and m=K*gamma-1>0. Any joint degree<=d-phase/affine competitor g with H(g)-K I(g)>=H(f)-K a(f)-epsilon has r<=epsilon/m in its one-phase normal form. Thus epsilon<m forces that reduced phase to be a signed character. Actual root maximality additionally requires I(f)=a(f). This is a scoped rigidity corollary, not a child-funding theorem or FEI bound.
